conventions.convention: Spatial coordinates have standard right-handed orientation; the Jacobian has entries (D_x u)ij = ∂xj ui, vector Laplacians act componentwise, and stress is −pI₃ + μ(D_xu + (D_xu)ᵀ).

The formal systems are pointwise mathematical equations. Velocity has continuous first time and first and second spatial partial derivatives; density is positive with continuous first time and spatial partial derivatives. No physical realization or solution existence is asserted.
S and C are the real parts of the exponential definitions of complex sine and cosine on real arguments, agreeing with real sine and cosine.

All scaling constants are positive. Incompressible pressure uses scale ρ₀U², while barotropic pressure uses scale ρ₀c² and offset P(ρ₀). Re = UL/ν and Ma = U/c; these transformations assert no asymptotic limit.

Acoustic phase is k·x − ωt with k ≠ 0. The acoustic dispersion iff requires A ≠ 0; zero amplitude solves the system for every ω. Rotating modes use b = e × a and signed frequency α = 2Ω·e, including α = 0 without division.

The vertical coordinate is positive upward, with bottom z = −h and mean surface z = 0. Parameters h, g, k are strictly positive, and ω is the positive square root of gk tanh(kh). Boundary derivatives extend continuously to both vertical endpoints.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the pointwise constant-density incompressible Navier–Stokes and steady Stokes systems, positive-density barotropic Euler system, rotating linear system, Cartesian differential operators, stress, circulation, flux, streamlines and material loops, with explicit regularity and optional SI interpretation.
Then S and C are differentiable on ℝ and satisfy S′(t)=C(t) and C′(t)=−S(t) for every real t.
For all a,b,c ∈ ℝ³, the Euclidean cross product satisfies a × (b × c) = b⟨a,c⟩ − c⟨a,b⟩.
For every real s ≥ 0, 0 ≤ s − tanh s ≤ s³/3 and 0 ≤ 1 − tanh s ≤ 2e^(−2s).

Under the stated positive scale substitutions and field regularity, the incompressible system is equivalent to its displayed dimensionless system with viscosity coefficient Re⁻¹; the barotropic equations transform exactly with pressure coefficient Ma⁻² and the displayed scaled potential term. No limit, error estimate, uniqueness or identification of solutions with different rescaled data is asserted.

For the stated acoustic mode with χ > 0, k ≠ 0 and A ≠ 0, the linear acoustic system holds exactly iff ω² = χ|k|²; A = 0 gives the zero solution for every ω. For χ < 0 the displayed exponentially growing modes solve the linear system. The displayed rotating fields solve the rotating linear system with signed frequency α = 2Ω·e and |α| ≤ 2|Ω|, including α = 0.

For h,g,k > 0 and real a, the displayed elevation and potential with ω = √(gk tanh(kh)) solve the stated finite-depth linear boundary problem. Their shallow squared-frequency and frequency relative errors are bounded by (kh)²/3, and their deep squared-frequency relative error is bounded by 2e^(−2kh), with all three errors nonnegative.

concerns.concern: The Example says “The dimensionless groups are” and includes ν = 1 m² s⁻¹ in that list. ν is dimensional kinematic viscosity; only Re and Ma are dimensionless here. The numerical calculation and displayed units are correct.

The circulation, volume-flux and resultant-force definitions suppress the time argument although u and σ are defined on I × Ω. Explicitly fixing t ∈ I and using u(t,·) and σ(t,·) would make these observables type-complete; the intended fixed-time interpretation is readily reconstructed.

alerts.finding: Fact F1 attributes to def-fd-x00 that “smooth scalar fields have commuting mixed partials.” That supplier defines Cartesian operators and regularity but does not state or prove equality of mixed partial derivatives. The smooth explicit potential makes this a standard missing justification, rather than a false conclusion; cite an adequate supplier or give the needed local calculation.

seams_checked.note: pthm-fd-px01-prediction F3 faithfully uses thm-fd-x01 as exact equation equivalence. Its physical branches meet the supplier hypotheses, use V = 0, and retain the exclusions of limits, existence and empirical validation.

The Navier–Stokes, Stokes, barotropic, stress and circulation conventions match def-fd-x00, with periodic lifts and inviscid equations defined separately where needed. The exception is thm-fd-x13 F1, which additionally attributes commuting mixed partials to that definition; see the alert.

Consumers preserve the steady Stokes omission of both time derivative and convection, the coefficient ν = μ/ρ₀, and the componentwise Laplacian. Higher-dimensional operators, periodic lifts and the separate interface equations are defined locally.

The rotating-stratified definition accurately identifies the Cartesian operators and classical regularity supplied by def-fd-x00. It explicitly supplies periodic lifts and the independent two-dimensional shallow-water formulation.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its current items define their torus calculus and coupled equations independently and contain no item-level citation to this batch. No stronger proposition is attributed to fd-x01.

The wall model preserves Cartesian conventions while defining forcing locally. The capillary theorem accurately quotes thm-fd-x03 for h,g,k > 0, supplies periodicity separately, and recovers its gravity mode at σ = 0. The underlying gravity-wave boundary problem and dispersion relation also match [Feddersen, equations (2.14)–(2.19)](https://falk.ucsd.edu/pdf/WavesLecture02_211A.pdf).
